clue.text: Boon finished filming, as covered in paper

parts.note: a boon is a gift or blessing
a film shoot that has finished is said to have wrapped

explanation.surface: An actor called Boon completes a shoot, and the set is papered over.
explanation.walkthrough: Boon looks like a name, as with the TV drama of that title, but it is just a common noun meaning a gift.
explanation.definitionFit: A present wrapped in decorative paper before it is handed over is described with this hyphenated adjective.

clue.text: Wave from guest shedding uniform by northern river

indicators.note: by means beside, so the pieces are set next to each other
shedding means casting off, so that letter is dropped

parts.note: taken as written
U is uniform in the NATO alphabet
the Ure is a river in North Yorkshire

explanation.surface: A guest out of uniform waves beside a river up north.
explanation.definitionFit: A wave of the hand is a gesture, a movement that conveys a message.

clue.text: Saucy novel

explanation.walkthrough: Saucy novel reads as a racy book, but novel is an adjective meaning new.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both cheekily forward, as in getting too familiar, and new or not seen before.

clue.text: Wag regularly incenses spectator

parts.note: a wag is a joker, a witty person

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every second letter is kept

parts.note: the even letters of the word

explanation.surface: A joker keeps annoying an onlooker.
explanation.walkthrough: The selection indicator sits before the word it acts on, though the surface makes it modify wag.
explanation.definitionFit: A witness is someone who sees an event happen, an onlooker or observer.

clue.text: Nicknames upset host going around yacht?

indicators.note: set upside down, a down entry is read from bottom to top
going around means surrounding, so one word wraps the other

parts.note: a host, as in a sea of faces, is a great number
to yacht is to sail, hence the question mark

explanation.surface: A host taking offence at being nicknamed after a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: Host means a multitude here, the same as a sea of something.
explanation.definitionFit: An alias is an assumed name, close to a nickname or pseudonym.

clue.text: Pauline's excitedly packing new cape

indicators.note: packing means holding inside, so the extra letter goes in among the others
acting excitedly is agitated behaviour, so the letters are thrown about

parts.note: taken as written without the apostrophe
N abbreviates new

explanation.surface: Pauline eagerly packs a brand-new cloak for a trip.
explanation.walkthrough: Cape reads as a garment Pauline is packing, but it is the headland.
explanation.definitionFit: A cape is a headland jutting into the sea, a kind of peninsula.

clue.text: Clear up bank, relatively messy

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to rid is to clear of something
a bank of seats is a tier or row

explanation.surface: Tidying a riverbank that has become rather messy.
explanation.walkthrough: Clear up reads as a phrasal verb meaning tidy, but up is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Relatively messy is a comparative: dirtier means more soiled or untidy than something else.

clue.text: Men sit occasionally next to hives? Most unwise

indicators.note: placing one piece beside another joins them end to end, with the earlier piece put after

parts.note: hives is an itchy skin rash

indicators.note: something done occasionally happens only now and then, so only every other letter is kept

parts.note: the even letters of the two words

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about men sitting beside beehives, judged a foolish idea.
explanation.walkthrough: Hives looks like beehives in the surface, but here it is the skin complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: Rash means reckless or ill-considered, so its superlative is the most reckless, the least wise.

clue.text: Spooner's concealing bunny in horsewoman's dress

indicators.note: Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the initial sounds trade places

parts.note: concealing means hiding, and a bunny is a rabbit; swap their first sounds

explanation.surface: A rider keeps a rabbit hidden in her outfit.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the traditional outfit worn by women for horse riding, especially riding side-saddle.

clue.text: Cuts affected regions

indicators.note: something affected has been changed or disturbed, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Budget cuts have hit certain parts of the country.
explanation.walkthrough: Cuts reads as a noun about spending, but it is a verb: to cut someone is to snub them.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut someone is to snub them deliberately, pretending not to see them, which is to pay them no attention.

clue.text: Alarm sirens going off in work by George!

indicators.note: something going off has gone bad or exploded, so the letters are scattered

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Alarms sounding at work, with an exclaimed By George!
explanation.walkthrough: By George! looks like an old exclamation; George Eliot was the pen name of Mary Ann Evans, author of this novel.
explanation.definitionFit: George Eliot wrote the 1861 novel about a lonely weaver, so it is one of her works.

clue.text: Wealth that's needed for Rolls

definitions.meaning: second meaning: the mixture a baker shapes into bread rolls

explanation.surface: You need to be rich to own a Rolls-Royce.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital R makes Rolls look like the luxury car, which fits the money sense; the bread sense needs the lower-case word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is slang for cash and also the flour-and-water paste baked into bread.

clue.text: Crucial German city hearing barring lawyer at last

parts.note: Essen is a city in the Ruhr

indicators.note: barring means excluding, so that letter is taken out

parts.note: a court hearing is a trial

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of the word before it

parts.note: the final letter of lawyer

explanation.surface: A court hearing in a German city that matters a great deal, held without a lawyer.
explanation.walkthrough: Hearing is not a sound clue here; it is a court hearing, which loses its R.
explanation.definitionFit: Crucial and essential are synonyms: both describe something absolutely necessary.

clue.text: Pesters half-cut news editor with foreign article

indicators.note: cut in half means only the first half of the word survives
with puts the pieces side by side in sequence

parts.note: taken as written, then halved
ED is the standard abbreviation for editor
les is the French plural definite article

explanation.surface: A drunk news editor annoys colleagues with a piece from abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: Half-cut is British slang for drunk, which the surface uses; the wordplay takes it literally.
explanation.definitionFit: To needle someone is to provoke or irritate them persistently, which is what pestering does.

clue.text: Bored by America, Prince in a state

indicators.note: something bored by another has a hole drilled into it with the other inside

parts.note: Prince Louis of Wales, a British royal
taken as written
taken as written
A abbreviates America

explanation.surface: A prince who is bored by America and in a bit of a state.
explanation.walkthrough: In a state looks like the end of the sentence; the in and a are wordplay, and only state defines. Prince Louis is a grandson of King Charles III.
explanation.definitionFit: Louisiana is one of the fifty US states, so it is an example of the definition.

clue.text: Silk scarves stuffed shirts

definitions.meaning: first meaning: square pieces of silk worn as headscarves
second meaning: stiff, conventional, old-fashioned people

explanation.surface: A list of clothing: silk scarves and padded shirts.
explanation.walkthrough: Stuffed shirts sounds like more clothing, but it is an idiom for pompous, conventional people.
explanation.definitionFit: Silk headscarves are sold as squares, and a square is also slang for an unfashionably conventional person.

clue.text: Minor snags unavoidable for Vespucci heading to the west

indicators.note: in an across entry, heading west means reading right to left
what is unavoidable for something is built into it, so the letters sit inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: The explorer Amerigo Vespucci, sailing west, was bound to meet small setbacks.
explanation.walkthrough: Heading looks like part of the voyage, but the letters straddle Vespucci and heading.
explanation.definitionFit: Hiccups is used informally for small, temporary problems or setbacks.

clue.text: Typical group of schoolkids, extremely idiotic

parts.note: a school class is a group of pupils

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its two ends, so only first and last letters stay

parts.note: the first and last letters

explanation.surface: A school class behaving in a typically silly way.
explanation.walkthrough: Extremely seems to intensify idiotic, but it is the selection signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A classic example is a typical, archetypal one, the textbook case.

clue.text: Background of audibly distinguished lines?

indicators.note: audibly means as heard, so the word is spelt as it sounds, not as it means

parts.note: distinguished in the sense of made out or spotted
RY abbreviates railway, a set of lines

explanation.surface: A query about the backdrop to lines spoken clearly on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: Lines suggests an actor's script, which fits the theatrical answer, but here it is railway lines.
explanation.definitionFit: Stage scenery is the painted backdrop behind the actors, the background to a play.

clue.text: Gardener on vacation with Pennsylvania relative

indicators.note: vacated means emptied, so the middle is cleared out and only the outside letters stay

parts.note: the first and last letters
with and and both mean together with
PA is the postal abbreviation for Pennsylvania

explanation.surface: A gardener holidays in Pennsylvania with a family member.
explanation.definitionFit: A grandfather is a family member, a relation two generations up.

clue.text: Lad's heart captivated by fantastic Danger Island

indicators.note: something captivated is held captive, so it sits inside the other letters
fantastic means fanciful and unreal, so the letters take an imaginative new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its middle letter

parts.note: the middle letter of lad

explanation.surface: A boy is enchanted by an adventure story called Danger Island.
explanation.definitionFit: Grenada is a Caribbean island nation, so it is an example of an island.

clue.text: Cleaner — lovely guy

parts.note: a dish is slang for an attractive person
to guy someone is to mock or tease them, as is to rag

explanation.surface: A cleaner described as a lovely man.
explanation.walkthrough: Guy looks like a noun for a man, but both pieces are other parts of speech: a dish, and the verb to guy.
explanation.definitionFit: A dishrag is a cloth for washing dishes, a cleaning tool.

clue.text: Supporter's front that is mostly red

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: front and brass both mean cheek or nerve
i.e. abbreviates id est, Latin for that is
taken as written, then shortened

explanation.surface: A political supporter whose public face is largely left-wing.
explanation.walkthrough: Front here means effrontery, the same nerve as brass neck; the 's is is, joining definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A bra is an undergarment that supports the bust, so it is literally a supporter.

clue.text: Curious time to back heavyweight boxer

indicators.note: going back means travelling in the opposite direction, so the joined letters are read in reverse

parts.note: curious in the prying sense
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A curious moment to put money on a big fighter.
explanation.walkthrough: Back looks like betting on the boxer, but it is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Mike Tyson was undisputed world heavyweight boxing champion, so he is an example of the definition.

clue.text: Measures item pipeline incorporates

indicators.note: to incorporate is to contain within, so the letters lie inside the preceding words

parts.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: Measures that an item of pipeline takes in.
explanation.walkthrough: Measures is used in its musical sense of tempo or time.
explanation.definitionFit: In music, tempi are speeds or time signatures, and measure is an old word for rhythm or tempo.

clue.text: Sort ape's bananas in reserve

indicators.note: bananas is slang for crazy, so the letters go wild and are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Organise the monkey's bananas and keep some back.
explanation.walkthrough: Bananas looks like fruit for the ape, but it is slang for mad and signals the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Something held in reserve is extra, available beyond what is needed now.

clue.text: Fan of a dreadful Republican seizing mic's lead

indicators.note: to seize something is to grab hold of it, so the earlier letters close around it

parts.note: taken as written
dire means dreadful
R abbreviates Republican

indicators.note: the lead of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of mic

explanation.surface: A supporter of an awful Republican politician who grabs the microphone.
explanation.walkthrough: The M goes inside after the first letter of the adjective, splitting it.
explanation.definitionFit: An admirer is someone who looks up to another, the same as a fan or devotee.

clue.text: Flags up the pole?

parts.note: surface reading: banners hoisted on a flagpole
setter's reading: flagstones that are up the pole, British slang for mad, so irregularly laid paving stones

explanation.walkthrough: Flags are flagstones, and up the pole is British slang for crazy, so the stones are laid in a wild pattern.
explanation.definitionFit: This garden surface is made of irregular broken slabs fitted together like a jigsaw rather than in rows.
